title: How do you achieve fault isolation (exception handling, circuit breaker, redundancy, microservice boundaries, failover, bulkhead, resource limits)?
shortTitle: How do you achieve fault isolation
keyPoints: Fault isolation means containing a failure to the smallest possible boundary so it cannot cascade into a system-wide outage.
Exception handling catches failures at the right layer and translates low-level errors into meaningful domain errors.
Microservice boundaries are structural firewalls: one service's failure cannot directly corrupt another's state.
Bulkheads partition shared resources like thread pools so one slow dependency cannot exhaust everything.
Circuit breakers isolate a failing dependency in time by failing fast instead of piling up requests.
Kubernetes resource limits ensure a memory leak or CPU hog in one pod only kills that pod, not its neighbors.
Fault isolation is defence in depth across space (bulkheads, boundaries), time (circuit breakers, timeouts), and location (redundancy, failover).

s1_definition.oneliner: Fault isolation means building firewalls into the system so a failure stays contained instead of taking everything down with it.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Exception handling** – Catch and handle failures at the right layer, translate low-level errors into meaningful domain responses, and never let exceptions propagate uncontrolled across boundaries.
- **Microservice boundaries** – Each service owns its data and communicates through well-defined interfaces, so a failure in one cannot corrupt another's state.
- **Bulkhead** – Partition shared resources like thread pools so one slow dependency cannot exhaust all threads, named after a ship's watertight compartments.
- **Circuit breaker** – Stop calling a failing dependency after a threshold, fail fast instead of piling up, and test recovery periodically.
- **Resource limits** – Kubernetes CPU and memory limits ensure a runaway container is throttled or killed, not allowed to starve neighbors.
s1_definition.analogy: Imagine the National Bank of India's head office is one giant open hall where every department shares the same desks and phone lines. If the loans team gets swamped and grabs every phone, the deposits team cannot work either. A fault-isolated bank instead has separate rooms with fire doors between them, each room with its own fixed set of phones and clerks, a rule that if a department stops answering you stop calling it, and duplicate rooms in another building ready to take over.

sections.s6_takeaway:
Fault isolation is about building firewalls into the system so that when something breaks, only that one thing is affected and the failure cannot cascade into a system-wide outage. The innermost layer is exception handling, where failures are caught at the right place and translated into meaningful domain errors. The structural layer is microservice boundaries: by splitting the system into services that each own their data, a failure in one cannot corrupt another's state.

Spatial isolation within a service comes from bulkheads. At National Bank of India, balance checks, transfers, and statement generation all shared one thread pool, and a slow statement service consumed every thread so even instant balance lookups could not run. The fix was giving each call type its own bounded pool, so a slow statement path exhausts only its own threads. Temporal isolation comes from circuit breakers that fail fast when a dependency is down, and resource limits in Kubernetes ensure a memory leak in one pod only kills that pod.

The complete picture is defence in depth across three dimensions: space (bulkheads, boundaries, resource limits), time (circuit breakers, timeouts), and location (redundancy, failover across zones). Pankaj designed the payment service at National Bank of India with all three: separate bulkheads for fraud checks and balance lookups, circuit breakers on every downstream call, resource limits per container, and replicas across three zones. When the fraud service went down, only the fraud bulkhead was affected and transfers kept flowing.

Remember one sentence: fault isolation is defence in depth across space, time, and location, so a fire, a flood, or a swamped dependency stays contained in one room instead of burning down the whole building.
